title: Cohort scaling runbook — rough + signal mapping
content:
Quick rough notes for a staggered cohort roll that focuses on scaling behavior rather than feature changes. Mostly a brain dump — single-author, expect follow-up edits.

Goal:
- Ramp a model flip (v2 -> v3) across client cohorts while preserving p95 latency and avoiding token-cost spikes.
- Detect regressions early with signal mapping tied to cohort size.

Assumptions / constraints:
- v3 uses new KV cache eviction that reduces memory per session but has a slower cold-start by ~30ms.
- Dedicated pool capacity sufficient for 20% of overall traffic; remaining traffic must go to hosted fallback variants.
- Some tenants (enterprise tier) pinned to v2 for contractual reasons.

Cohort design (rough):
1) Shadow cohort (internal only): 0% traffic, mirrored requests to v3 for metrics and quality evals. Duration: 48h.
2) Micro-cohort A (alpha clients): 0.5% traffic, clients with stable historically low-variance latencies. Warmup window: 30m
3) Micro-cohort B (beta): 2% traffic, mixed clients (mobile/web). Warmup: 1h
4) Ramp cohort (gamma): 8% traffic, gradually add clients by weight over 6h windows
5) Broad roll: move remaining eligible traffic in 4x steps (25% increments) with 24h observation per step

Warmup sequencing and priming notes:
- For each cohort, pre-warm by sending 5k synthetic low-context requests (small prompt) to populate KV caches. TODO script: synthetic-warmup.sh (see linked PR).
- Ensure prefix caching is enabled in routing policy for cohort IDs.

Safety signals (priority ordered):
- Latency: p95 endpoint latency increase > 10% relative to baseline -> hold and investigate
- Error rate: 5xx spike > 0.5% absolute (or 3x baseline) -> immediate throttle to 0 for cohort
- Token cost per request: sudden >15% increase -> flag (cost team review)
- Model quality regressions: BLEU/ROUGE for eval set drops > 2 points OR manual review flags repeated hallucination patterns -> pause
- Memory/GPU OOMs or evictions > 2 occurrences in 1h -> emergency rollback

Telemetry mapping (where to look):
- infra/latency/service.p95, service.p50 (tags: model=v3, cohort=gamma)
- infra/errors/5xx-rate (group by region, model)
- billing/token_per_req (rolling-avg, 5m)
- cache/hit_rate (by model, warmup windows)
- kv/eviction_count (per pod)
- quality/eval_score (daily batch job, compare to baseline)

Automatic actions (ideas):
- If latency p95 > 10% for 15m: scale up dedicated pool + hold ramp (notify #deploy-alerts)
- If 5xx-rate breach: circuit-break cohort to 0% and route to v2 fallback (automated via routing policy)
- If token cost jumps: temporarily reduce max tokens for cohort to soft cap (config by route)

Manual gating checklist (must confirm before each ramp step):
- [ ] Shadow telemetry stable for 48h (no signal breaches)
- [ ] Warmup synthetic traffic completed and cache hit_rate >= 30% baseline
- [ ] No uncaught OOMs in the last 6h
- [ ] Quality eval shows no >2 point regression on eval set
- [ ] On-call SRE ack on escalation plan and pager rotation

Rollback quick commands (ops cheat):
- Throttle cohort to 0 (API): curl -X POST $ROUTER/api/v1/route/throttle -d '{"cohort":"gamma","pct":0}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'
- Pin client back to v2 (client-level): curl -X POST $API/clients/{id}/pin -d '{"model":"v2"}'
- Force fallback routing (global): POST /api/v1/routing/force-fallback model=v2 -> routes all non-enterprise to v2 until cleared

Open questions / unresolved:
- What is the safe synthetic warmup request shape for long-context clients? (need to run profiling)
- Should enterprise tenants be allowed to opt-in to v3 for early access? (legal check for contractual pinning)
- How do we surface quality drift if it is subtle and distributed across prompts? (slices/alerts?)

Post-mortem anchors (if rollback happens):
- Timeline capture: when ramp started, first breach, actions taken, who acked
- Snapshot telemetry: collect 30m pre and post breach for p50/p95, 5xx, token cost, cache hit
- Preserve debug logs (model and routing traces) with trace ids for failing requests

Notes-to-self (quick):
- Keep warmup under low-cost synthetic tokens; do not let warmup exceed 100k tokens per cohort for initial test
- Coordinate with Cost lead (Marco) before broad roll (linked artifact PR mentions cost knobs)
- Add small canary key to requests (x-canary-id) so we can filter logs without tying to tenant ids

Immediate next steps (today):
- [ ] Draft short runbook for SRE on-call with the above quick commands (deadline: EOD)
- [ ] Add synthetic warmup script to PR #879 (assign to Marco)
- [ ] Create a small eval prompt set for alpha cohort (ask Applied ML for 200 prompts)

If this is useful, will expand into a formal playbook with diagrams and exact run commands. For now: messy, actionable, and portable.

-- Priya
